Ask the operator (AskUserQuestion) and file docs/ddflow/decisions/dsh.md. Recommended defaults in brackets. (1) Tier: [tier 2 fixtures-only now; tier 1 live smoke only after DSH-lane proves a headless run with a stub endpoint]. (2) Where adopt writes config: [only a ddflow-owned overlay file in the repo plus a printed launch line (dsh --profile

--patch .ddflow/harness/dsh.cordis.yml); never edit $DSH_HOME profiles without per-agent consent]. (3) Hooks: [mount the opt-in experimental hooks-claude-code bridge from the overlay, fail open; claim/lease enforcement via PreToolUse only when the bridge is verified loaded, else reported unavailable]. (4) Lane permission: [lane-private DSH_HOME, workspace-write sandbox, approval resolved by the ddflow permission broker over ACP; headless lanes only with DSH_PERMISSION_MODE=danger-full-access inside a disposable worktree/container, operator opt-in]. (5) Credentials: [env only, never argv or committed; lane-private DSH_HOME so the user's stored keys are not read]. (6) Telemetry: [dsh product telemetry is Desktop-only and opt-in; record, do not toggle]. (7) Reviewer role: [no dsh reviewer; keep direct OpenAI-compatible reviewers, because ddflow review needs a diff in and a verdict out, not an agent loop]. (8) Review independence: [family is the model family of the run, not the harness: a dsh run on a DeepSeek model is family deepseek and cannot be reviewed by lan-deepseek-*]. (9) Ship ddflow as a dsh bundle package: [defer; overlay first]. CORRECTION: item (8) is informational: independence is judged from the model declared at session start, so the operator only needs to confirm that dsh sessions declare their model; no harness-level family exists. Hold edges to P-doc-templates, P-docs-generic, P-roadmap, P-docs-search removed 2026-10-22: the operator answered this task's questions (recorded verbatim in the session) and decisions are docs-only; the hold protected core/docs waves, not an answered decision.

**Where the doc is:** `docs/ddflow/research/mcp-builder-guide.md`. Items are marked verified, unverified or theoretical. I read the 2026-07-28 spec pages for tools, transports, pagination and the ToolAnnotations schema. I did not open the best-practices page or the Inspector pages, so the Inspector CLI flags are marked unverified.

**Ratings** (15 practices in the doc):
- **Met:**
  - Prefix and naming: all tools are `ddflow_*`.
  - Concise descriptions: mean 275 characters.
  - Workflow tools plus primitives: the tool-diet phase keeps 9 hot singles and folds the rest into families.
  - Shared infrastructure: one outcome-to-result path, plus CLI/MCP parity tests.
  - Deterministic tool order.
  - stdio transport. HTTP is not applicable, since ddflow is a local per-repo server.
- **Partly:**
  - Pagination and bounds: only 5 reads are bounded; `ddflow_list` has `limit`/`offset`.
  - Actionable errors: did-you-mean hints and `isError` are good, but "missing required argument" quotes no description.
  - Input validation: missing and unknown arguments are refused; types, enums and ranges are not.
  - Self-check: the conformance tests are strong, but nothing spawns the real server and lints what it advertises.
  - outputSchema and structuredContent: implemented but off by default on purpose. Research Rd25385ec42 measured over 10 KB extra in `tools/list`. I queued nothing.
- **Gap:**
  - Tool annotations: none are emitted. The 2026-07-28 spec defaults are worst case (destructive and open-world), so every ddflow tool looks that way to a client.
  - Input constraints: 0 of 488 properties carry enum, minimum or pattern. `Param.schema_enum` exists but is switched off everywhere.
  - Examples: 19 of 488 descriptions have one.
  - LLM-usability evals: none exist.
- **Deliberate deviation, kept:** an unknown tool returns `isError` instead of a JSON-RPC error, so the model sees the did-you-mean.

**Queued:** phase `P-mcp-practices`, with 10 tasks tagged `feature,ddflow-gap`.
- Eval set (design is in the doc; 10 read-only questions on a fixture project):
  - `MCPP-eval-fixture`
  - `MCPP-eval-questions` (needs the fixture)
  - `MCPP-eval-oracle` (a scripted, no-LLM check that runs in the normal suite)
  - `MCPP-eval-harness` (opt-in LLM runner)
- `MCPP-effect-class`: one read/additive/destructive table for every command (needs `MTD-family-spec`).
- `MCPP-annotations` (needs `MCPP-effect-class`, `MTD-profiles`).
- `MCPP-input-schema` (needs `MTD-family-spec`).
- `MCPP-result-bounds` (needs the fixture).

data.body:
Writes .ddflow/harness/dsh.cordis.yml with an insert patch: id ddflow dsh-mcp-client (stdio, command ddflow mcp, cwd the project, env DDFLOW_AGENT/identity explicit because stdio children lose ambient DSH_* and any name matching KEY/PASSWORD/SECRET/TOKEN), id ddflow-hooks dsh-hooks-claude-code with configPath .ddflow/harness/dsh.hooks.json, projectDir, defaultTimeoutMs small. Prints the one-line launch command; offers (never does unasked) the merge into a profile patch. Idempotent twice-run, uninstall restores, record in the install manifest. Failure modes reported not hidden: hooks config unreadable means dsh logs a warning and runs NO hooks (silent), so the overlay also writes a canary the verify task reads.

PROBE (DSH-facts, dsh-probe.md): new rows need '- insert: [ {id,name,config} ]'; an id override replaces the whole config; unknown id only warns. The hooks bridge in the overlay must be named by absolute path to .../dsh-hooks-claude-code/lib/index.js (a bare name resolves from the profile dir and fails; failure only warns on stderr and the agent starts without hooks). Install a version-matched copy (@next = 0.2.1-rc.2, NOT latest 0.0.1-rc.5, which dsh disables). Pass ddflow env explicitly in the mcp row env.

Reuse the claude normalizer/emitter where the payload is identical; add a thin dsh mapping for tool names (matcher is the dsh tool name) and for exit-code-2 block semantics (Codex dialect cannot ask; Claude dialect can). Compaction handoff and session end have no hook: ladder levels fall to first-call/mcp-text, reported by harness show. Test that a SessionStart injection that arrives after turn 1 is detected by the first-call brief.

PROBE: tool_name is dsh's own lowercase name (bash, read, write, edit, glob, grep, web_fetch, web_search, subagent...) and mcp__ddflow__<tool>; tool_input for bash is {description,command}; tool_response is a string; transcript_path is always empty; SessionStart context arrived before turn 1 even with a 4 s hook (headless); PreToolUse exit 2 blocks with the stderr as the error. Hook env inherits the launcher env, so CLAUDE_* from a parent Claude Code leaks in. Fixtures: tests/fixtures/dsh_probe/hook_payloads.ndjson.

Uses dsh --profile

--patch --dump-config (does not boot the model; read the schema-dump safety note) to prove the rows are composed; headless run with a stub endpoint to prove tools/hook reach; checks failOnStartupError false means an MCP connect failure only logs, so a missing tools list is detected and reported. Not installed or not runnable: unavailable. PROBE: Node >= 22.19 is not sufficient: dsh refused the nix node v24.21.0 ('host preparation failed: node-addon-require-builtin unsupported') and ran on /usr/bin/node v24.22.0. Verify must boot dsh (--dump-config does not catch it; --version and --help passed on both), and must parse stderr for 'did not activate' / 'disabling profile plugin row' / 'entry ... not found'.

Format only partly verified: dsh-session-persistence-jsonl, 'default zstd-compressed session log' per hooks README; session events documented in docs/persistence-catalog.md. DSH-facts records a real file. Read-only; secrets redacted per B-am-ingest.

PROBE: layout $DSH_HOME/sessions/<cwd, / as ->, wrapped in -->/session-<uuid>/session.v4.jsonl.zstd (+ empty session.lock); 'zstd -dc' gives JSONL {type,seq,time,data}; types session, request/header (provider+model+tools), assistant/message (source.provider/model), tool/call, tool/result, hook/invoked, hook/result. The model is in the log, so the family can be attributed.

dsh lists every MCP tool as a native tool (mcp__ddflow__*, tools appear before the first turn, no tool_search found), so the default for clientInfo dsh-mcp-client is the lean profile from MTD-profiles. Doctor: instruction files rendered size vs the 65536-byte baseline budget (broader files dropped before the most specific is truncated); the first-turn token estimate feeds LS-measure.

PROBE: first request with the full ddflow MCP surface is about 154k chars (about 38k tokens) vs 24k chars native: 123 mcp__ddflow__* tools = 115k chars of tool JSON, plus the server instructions (about 13k chars) in the system prompt. No deferral; tools are present on request 1. dsh declares no client capabilities.

Adds the row into SU-client-table's table and the probe (not an edit of mcp-client-matrix.md beyond the row); the first-turn behaviour (tools appear before the first turn; new tools after list_changed re-sync with the previous generation kept on failure) and the facade-mode consequence: list_changed is honoured, so soft upgrade works without facade.

PROBE: dsh speaks 2026-07-28 stateless: first message server/discover with _meta (protocolVersion, clientInfo dsh-mcp-client 0.0.1, empty clientCapabilities), no initialize; ddflow answered. list_changed at runtime not exercised.

dsh --profile headless --patch <overlay> --json "<task>" (or the task on stdin), events session/status/text/thinking/tool_call/tool_result/final, exit 0/1, --session-id to continue; one task per process, no steering mid-run (use ACP for that). Env: DSH_HOME lane-private, DSH_PERMISSION_MODE per DSH-decide, provider key by env never argv. Failure modes: tokenless run exits 1 with dsh: <code>: <message>; an approval ask with no answerer is unavailable (fail closed) so the lane stalls into denials, not hangs; 32 KiB line cap truncates events (use final for the answer).

PROBE: headless exits 0 even when a tool is denied (hook or sandbox) or an escalation has no approval channel; exit 1 only for run errors such as MISSING_CREDENTIAL. A lane must read the tool_result statuses and final event, not only the exit code. web_fetch/web_search are on by default in headless.

Option (d): a package whose cordis.patch.yml layer is the overlay and whose dsh.profile manifest lists the bundle; installed with dsh plugin --profile

add . Executable third-party code in the user's profile, supply-chain surface and engines.dsh floor; held until DSH-decide says yes. Nothing is published by this task. PROBE: telemetry is NOT Desktop-only: base composition mounts session-telemetry-otel (FEEDBACK_ONLY default, exporter dsh-otel-collector.deepseeksvc.com, DSH_TELEMETRY_MODE=DISABLED turns it off). Operator decision: record, do not toggle.

Found by DSH-decide. An agent whose MCP connection sits in a worktree bound to item X is refused for item Y with 'cd [REDACTED:path] && ddflow claim Y' or --no-worktree; an MCP-only agent can do neither, and --no-worktree is wrong for a code task. The claim tool should offer to create Y's own tree (as the CLI from the primary does) when asked, or the refusal should name the MCP-reachable route. Worked around with the CLI from the primary checkout.

chunk_findings.detail: The task intent explicitly requires recording `--dump-config-schema` or marking it unavailable if it could not be run. This change records `--dump-default-config` in `tests/fixtures/dsh_probe/dump-default-config.headless.yml`, but the manifest contains no `--dump-config-schema` fixture and this document never mentions that required schema dump nor marks it UNKNOWN/unavailable, so the required probe fact is silently omitted.
chunk_findings.location: docs/ddflow/research/dsh-probe.md:5 (How it was run / Still UNKNOWN)
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/research/dsh-probe.md:5 (How it was run / Still UNKNOWN)

chunk_findings.detail: Line 36 states “A session title request is sent to the model as a second, tool-less request on every run”, but the same document’s “Exit codes and events” fact says a missing-key run exits 1 with a `turn_end` event whose reason is `error` and an empty `final.text`; that run never reaches a successful first model response, so no second title request can occur. The word “every run” is therefore false for the missing-credential run already recorded in the same report.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/research/dsh-probe.md:36

chunk_findings.detail: The changed note says “Nothing in this document was run,” but the same file’s “First-turn token cost with ddflow” row now records “MEASURED in chars with a stub.” That measurement came from running dsh, so the statement is false and makes the document internally inconsistent about what is run-derived.
chunk_findings.location: docs/ddflow/research/dsh.md “Nothing in this document was run”
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/research/dsh.md “Nothing in this document was run”

chunk_findings.detail: The row reports “about 154k chars (about 38k tokens)” as the first-turn token cost with ddflow while its own note says “dsh's own system prompt and tool declarations were not counted.” Since the system prompt and tool declarations are part of the first turn, that figure cannot be the first-turn token cost; the row overstates an incomplete fixture measurement as a resolved fact.
chunk_findings.location: docs/ddflow/research/dsh.md row “First-turn token cost with ddflow”
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/research/dsh.md row “First-turn token cost with ddflow”

chunk_findings.detail: The file name says `headless_pretooluse_exit2`, but the recorded NDJSON describes a successful run: `turn_end` has `"reason":{"kind":"completed"}` and `final` contains `"text":"stub done"`. A reader using this fixture to verify the intended exit-code-2 behavior (the change’s stated goal is to record exit codes) will see no exit code 2 and no PreToolUse-exit-2 termination; line 10-11 assert normal completion. This contradicts the filename and fails to record the PreToolUse exit-2 scenario it claims.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/dsh_probe/headless_pretooluse_exit2.ndjson:10-11

chunk_findings.detail: `"matcher": "*"` is not a valid Claude Code/dsh hook matcher: Claude Code bridge matcher values are regexes, and `*` has no preceding atom, so it either fails config validation or never matches. To match every tool this must be `""` or `".*"`. As checked in, this config cannot reproduce the `PreToolUse`/`PostToolUse` rows in `hook_payloads.ndjson`, which are claimed to have been captured using this hooks config.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/dsh_probe/hooks_example.json:3-4

chunk_findings.detail: The file is named and intended as an MCP handshake fixture, but the first client message uses `method: "server/discover"` and nests `protocolVersion`/`clientInfo`/`clientCapabilities` under `params._meta`. MCP handshake requires an `initialize` request with those values at the params level, followed by an `initialize` response; this file contains neither. Given a standard MCP server or MCP-validating consumer, line 1 returns a JSON-RPC `Method not found` error, so the subsequent `tools/list` and `tools/call` exchanges in lines 3-6 would never occur.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/dsh_probe/mcp_handshake.ndjson:1

chunk_findings.detail: The `tools/list` response (`s2c`, id 0) returns `{"tools_count":123, "tool_names":[ ... ], "tools_json_chars":109750}` and omits the required `tools` array. MCP `tools/list` results must contain a `tools` array of tool definitions; a compliant client or test consuming this line gets no tools or a validation error, so the fixture cannot establish “whether tools appear before the first turn” as the probe intends.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/dsh_probe/mcp_handshake.ndjson:4

chunk_findings.detail: The committed fixture leaves literal `<SCRATCH>` placeholders in the MCP client `args` (line 24), `cwd` (line 25), hook module path (line 27), `configPath` (line 29), and `projectDir` (line 30). Since the manifest describes this file as a recorded fixture under `tests/fixtures/dsh_probe/`, a clean test that applies the overlay will ask DSH to spawn `python3` with argument `<SCRATCH>/tools/mcp_proxy.py` and `cwd: <SCRATCH>/dshwork`; that literal directory does not exist, so the MCP client and hooks bridge fail to start and the recorded NDJSON fixtures cannot be reproduced. The actual recorded scratch path (or an explicit substitution step outside a fixture) is required.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/dsh_probe/overlay_example.cordis.patch.yml:24

chunk_findings.detail: The sentence “A session title request is sent to the model as a second, tool-less request on every run” is contradicted by the same document’s missing-credential result: `headless_missing_credential.ndjson` exits 1 with `dsh: MISSING_CREDENTIAL` and produces `final.text` empty, meaning dsh never gets a successful credential check and cannot send the second model request. “Every run” is therefore wrong for that recorded input; it should be limited to runs that reach a model call.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/research/dsh-probe.md:36

chunk_findings.detail: Both `PreToolUse` and `PostToolUse` entries use `"matcher": "*"` (lines 4 and 5). Claude Code hook matchers are regular expressions, and `"*"` is not a valid regular expression: `new RegExp("*")` throws `SyntaxError: Nothing to repeat`, so config loading aborts before any PreToolUse/PostToolUse hook can run. That contradicts `hook_payloads.ndjson`, whose recorded PreToolUse/PostToolUse events are supposed to have been produced with this config, making the fixture set unreproducible from the checked-in example.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/dsh_probe/hooks_example.json:4

chunk_findings.detail: The transcript is not a valid MCP handshake. It opens with `method: "server/discover"` instead of MCP’s required `initialize`, never exchanges `notifications/initialized`, and the `tools/list` result on line 4 omits the mandatory `tools` array, returning only custom `tools_count`/`tool_names`/`tools_json_chars` fields. A standards-compliant MCP client replaying this fixture would fail to initialize and would see zero advertised tools, so line 5’s `tools/call ddflow_brief` is impossible from the recorded state. This does not demonstrate the intended MCP handshake.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/dsh_probe/mcp_handshake.ndjson:1

A reader of this document is told both that every row below line 15 was not run and that one row below it was measured, so the blanket statement is false and mislabels the measured row.
